Tessa / team —

Adding technical detail so the draft synthesis aligns with Zenith’s review needs. Below is an extract we propose to include in the final 2–3 page submission; I’ll ship the fuller control matrix and evaluation regimen as attachments.

1) NIST AI RMF mapping (summary)
- Identify: asset inventory (models, datasets), model fingerprinting, version metadata in our control plane.
- Protect: encrypted storage (KMS), role-based access, tokenization for PII, and data retention policies configurable per-customer (Private & Dedicated).
- Detect: drift detectors, anomaly scanners on output distributions, and prompt-anchored regression tests.
- Respond: automated model rollback, canarying by traffic slice, and incident triage runbooks.
- Recover: versioned artifacts, KV cache snapshots for warm restores, and documented recovery SLAs for Dedicated customers.

2) EU AI Act positioning (summary)
- High-risk designation: Redwood treats regulated verticals with a conservative baseline: explicit documentation, mandatory human oversight hooks, and extended audit retention when required by contract. For customers subject to the Act, we provide artifact exports (evaluation reports, risk assessments, and model specification docs) and optional on-prem/private deployment.

3) Continuous evaluation & regression approach (practical regimen)
- Onboarding: acceptance bench of held-out test slices + adversarial prompt set provided by customer.
- Continuous: daily lightweight health checks (token-level latency, percentile latency, cost spikes) and weekly quality sampling across representative prompts.
- Regression signals: automatic alert if (a) top-line utility metrics degrade >2% relative to baseline on customer-supplied key prompts, (b) hallucination rate increases beyond defined threshold, or (c) regression tests fail on golden prompts.
- Escalation: auto-create ticket in Jira, notify CS and SRE; initiate canary rollback if regression persists across 3 consecutive runs.
- Forensics & audit: immutable audit logs for model inference (request id, model version, routing policy), timestamped eval snapshots, and cryptographically signed evaluation manifests when required.

Attachments included: eval-regimen-v1.pdf (detailed regimen), control-matrix.csv (mapping rows). I’ve kept thresholds conservative; we can tune to Zenith’s acceptance criteria.
